reason: CSP with 'unsafe-inline' for scripts and styles: Next.js hydrates the page with inline scripts, next-themes sets the theme with one and the accent colour is an inline style. A nonce would need every page rendered per request. The rest of the policy (no framing, no plugins, same-origin connections, a fixed list of image hosts and form targets) is what protects the interface; see src/lib/security-headers.ts.

A form that is a server action carries no CSRF token: Next.js refuses an action called from another origin and a form cannot set the header an action needs. The csrf suite of qa/security plays this against the real image (another site, a plain form on another site, null origin) and checks that nothing changes.

SQL injection reported on the forms that are server actions (the event form: every field, including the internal fields of the action, $ACTION_REF_1 and $ACTION_1:0). The rule compares the page for a condition that is true and one that is false, with no evidence of its own (the report has an empty evidence and medium confidence) and the answer of a server action carries data that changes from one call to the next. Nothing in src/ builds SQL from a string (Prisma binds every value, qa-rules forbids the rest), and the sql suite of qa/security plays the same pairs against the real form: a text is stored as typed, a field with a fixed set of values changes nothing beyond the event, and the outcome never depends on whether the condition is true.
